mechanisms.evidence: Seven distinct exclusive opportunity claim files were created from the same /wc lane; no manual numbered prompt was encoded in those claim identities.
One create-only claim path per observed opportunity; no duplicate exclusive claim file exists for the seven claimed opportunities.
O-WBOOT-SPEC-V1 return records two lost create-only races (BIG09 and Alumnos), no overwrite, reload, then successful claim of WBOOT.

All seven have durable run artifacts and WBOOT explicitly records STARTED-before-substantive-work. Wave1 lacks a uniform independent event receipt proving the ordering for every worker; v2 /wc now requires context/acceptance receipt before execution.
All seven observed claimed opportunities have durable RETURNs and terminal DONE runs that reference their return path.
WBOOT -> PROPOSALS is a same-session second opportunity; BIG13 -> POSTRETURN records the second-claim budget being used. Both second runs terminate and do not claim a third.

Workers voluntarily stopped when unrelated/fresh work was better assigned elsewhere and POST_RETURN spec forbids same-worker independent criticism, but no dedicated critic handoff canary has yet completed.
Observed worker run contracts restrict writes to claim + own run + own return. Recovery/discovery/spec workers report no shared authority-head mutation.

Wave1 uses manually declared read_scope, not generated L0/L1/L2 Context Receipts. Therefore Context Fabric must not be described as operational. /wc v2 now requires a context/acceptance receipt for new workers.
BIG09/BIG13 recovery was parent-authorized one-off recovery. Generic stale detection/reclaim/supersession has not been exercised.
Current canary queues were seeded by the parent. No generation N+1 has yet been compiled automatically from returns/proposals/incidents/critic findings.
Collision/self-assignment evidence is promising but Context Fabric, stale/retry, recursive Planner, critic/verification and recovery canaries remain open.
